solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Succeed in taking one's leave

definitions.meaning: to succeed is to do well, to get on happily
a leave-taking or goodbye is the noun sense

explanation.surface: Someone manages to leave on a good note.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'fare well' means prosper, and run together it is the word for a parting goodbye.

clue.text: A danger out east at this time of the year

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for east is taken away from the word for danger

parts.note: a peril is a danger
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A seasonal warning that some hazard is gone from the eastern region now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' means the letter for east leaves the word for danger; 'this time of the year' is the month the clue was published, a vague but fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A month of spring is a time of year, the clue pointing to it as 'this' time.

clue.text: Academic angrily cautioned a pupil

indicators.note: something done angrily is agitated and disordered, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: L stands for learner, a pupil driver's plate

explanation.surface: A professor scolds a student in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angrily' rearranges CAUTIONED and A to EDUCATIONA; L, the learner's sign, ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe matters of schooling and instruction.

clue.text: Point to member twirling cane with style

parts.note: E is a compass point, east
a leg is a limb or member of the body

indicators.note: twirling spins the walking stick round, so its letters turn into a new order

explanation.surface: A dandy points a foot and spins a walking stick with panache.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace and refinement of manner are synonyms here.

clue.text: Post-offices?

parts.note: not places selling stamps but offices where 'posts', jobs, were found for the unemployed

explanation.surface: Apparently just the places where mail is handled.
explanation.walkthrough: Post here means a job; these were the old British state job centres.
explanation.definitionFit: Government employment bureaux handed out situations, or posts, to job seekers.

clue.text: Mount and start on a journey

definitions.meaning: to mount a gem or picture is to display it to advantage, to show it up

explanation.surface: A rider climbs onto a horse and begins travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A setting enhances a jewel; departing travellers likewise begin by leaving.

clue.text: Waterlogged turf needs study

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: A soggy lawn needs looking at.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked through with water, as saturated ground is.

clue.text: Contraction of credit, we hear, can be painful

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: 'on tick' is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: A credit squeeze, people say, can hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contraction' is not economic: it is a twitch of a muscle, and 'can be painful' adds that some (tic douloureux) hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: An involuntary muscle spasm or twitch is a contraction.

clue.text: Priceless old weapon employed by no-one in particular

parts.note: something priceless in the sense of costing nothing is free
a lance is a medieval knight's spear

explanation.surface: An invaluable antique weapon was used by an anonymous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-employed worker sells services to many clients, with no single employer.

clue.text: Wake up artist retired alongside the river

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the artist's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A retired painter is roused beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir or rouse someone from sleep.

clue.text: Robed and venerable monk shuffled the deck

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian

indicators.note: shuffled, like cards, means the deck's letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A monk in his habit deals cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed up or adorned, as someone clothed in robes is.

clue.text: Mid-off on field in repulsive jumper

indicators.note: mid picks the central letter of the word off

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at mid-off is out in the field in an ugly sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position; here 'Mid-' takes F from 'off'. 'jumper' looks like a British sweater but is a leaping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasitic insect that leaps is a jumper, and an unwelcome one.

clue.text: A smart point of view in a tight corner

parts.note: cute can mean clever or smart
an angle is a perspective or point of view

explanation.surface: A clever outlook when someone is in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tight corner' sounds like a predicament, but it means a sharp corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner of less than ninety degrees is sharply narrow, hence tight.

clue.text: They embrace the cloth before grace

definitions.text: They embrace the cloth before grace

parts.words: They embrace the cloth before grace
parts.note: the cloth sounds like the clergy, but it is a table linen held in a circle, set out before grace at dinner

explanation.surface: Seemingly clergy hugged before saying a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' usually means the clergy; here it is a dinner serviette.
explanation.definitionFit: Circular holders encircle folded serviettes on a table laid for a meal.

clue.text: I'd come upset about something commonplace

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a trivial matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary and unremarkable, of middling quality.

clue.text: I had got back into new routine of learning

indicators.note: into tells us the reversed pair goes inside the other letters
new means the routine's letters are made afresh in a different order
got back means returned, so the contraction is read the other way

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone returns to a fresh study regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got back' reverses the contraction for 'I had', 'new' rearranges the routine's letters to ERUTION, and 'into' places the reversed pair inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship or deep knowledge is learning.

clue.text: Shut up and write a letter

parts.note: to pen is to write
T is simply a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An instruction to be quiet and compose a letter instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' is not 'be quiet' but confined.
explanation.definitionFit: Confined or penned in, as with emotions kept inside.

clue.text: Sir John's employees on the river

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the employees come next to the river's name

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a staff is the body of employees

explanation.surface: A knight's workers are out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat knight; the Fal is a Cornish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic knight is named Sir John, so the surname belongs to him.

clue.text: Change the course of a revolution

definitions.meaning: to change direction, as a verb
a single rotation or spin, as a noun

explanation.surface: Altering the direction of an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Veering changes direction; one rotation of a wheel is one revolution.

clue.text: It's instrumental in having wine around

indicators.note: around says the wine encloses the little word in

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine

explanation.surface: Someone played a key part in getting wine passed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumental' means a musical instrument, not influential.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind is literally a musical instrument, so it is instrumental.

clue.text: Fire when an explosive's not set?

indicators.note: not removes the letters for set from the explosive

parts.note: gelignite is a blasting explosive
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: Should one shoot when a bomb is unarmed?
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something is to set it alight, kindle it.

clue.text: They're responsible for the kids, but not without a nanny

definitions.text: They're responsible for the kids, but not without a nanny

parts.words: They're responsible for the kids, but not without a nanny
parts.note: kids are young goats and a nanny is a female goat; the males father kids only with a nanny

explanation.surface: Fathers who cannot raise children without a childminder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' and 'nanny' read as children and a childminder, but are young and female goats.
explanation.definitionFit: Male goats sire the kids, with the help of the nanny goat.

clue.text: Takes things the wrong way?

parts.note: taking possessions wrongly, by theft, rather than taking offence

explanation.surface: Someone is easily offended.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means misunderstands; here it is literal theft.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief takes property unlawfully, the wrong way to acquire it.

clue.text: Sailor stood up to embrace washed-out master from East Africa

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug, so the reversed sailor surrounds the pale letters
in a down clue stood up means written upwards, so the sailor reads backwards

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
wan means pale, washed-out

explanation.surface: A sailor rises to hug a pale boss in Kenya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood up' turns AB into BA in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swahili term of respect for a boss or sir in colonial East Africa.

clue.text: The author is not in

definitions.meaning: in cricket the side not batting, not 'in', is in the field

explanation.surface: The writer is away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the side batting is 'in'; the other side is out in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones; a cricket team not batting is out in the field.

clue.text: Sign nothing below the French

indicators.note: below in a down clue puts the zero beneath the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
O is the digit zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing signed under the French flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lion is a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Garden-flower periodical

definitions.meaning: a plant that lives for one year only
a book or magazine published once a year

explanation.surface: A gardening magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant completing its life in a year; a yearbook is a yearly publication.

clue.text: A call for repeated effort

parts.note: an audience shout asking performers to perform again

explanation.surface: A demand to try again.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre audience's cry for an extra performance, a repeat.

clue.text: Equestrian ability acquired by a large majority

definitions.meaning: a rider who sits securely on a horse has a secure position in the saddle
a parliamentary constituency won with a big majority

explanation.surface: Good horsemanship wins by a landslide.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm riding posture; and an electoral constituency held so comfortably it is unlikely to change hands.
